2607.17879.title: Exploratory and Assimilating Reflection: Reflective Recall Cycle for Long-term Memory
2607.17879.paper_summary: LLM-based autonomous agents require external memory to overcome their statelessness and limited context window for long-term interaction and dynamic knowledge reasoning. However, existing memory retrieval methods often lack adaptability and sample efficiency, and struggle to retrieve the right mixture of memories from heterogeneous stores. We propose Exploratory-Assimilating Reflection (EAR), a framework for high initial retrieval performance and sample-efficient adaptation. EAR combines two mechanisms: Exploratory Reflection, which performs iterative search to bootstrap retrieval and collect useful experiences for each query, and Assimilating Reflection, which replays these experiences from an Experience Buffer to refine a global reranker more efficiently than methods relying only on immediate rewards. Experiments show that EAR improves retrieval by up to 17.9% over the baseline retriever on two long-term dialogue benchmarks. We also show that EAR is highly sample-efficient and robust to noisy feedback.
2607.17879.paper_summary_zh: LLM 基礎的自主代理需要外部記憶來克服其無狀態性和有限的上下文窗口，以便進行長期互動和動態知識推理。<lb/>然而，現有的記憶檢索方法往往缺乏適應性和樣本效率，並且難以從異質存儲中檢索到正確的記憶混合。<lb/>我們提出了探索性同化反思（EAR），這是一個高初始檢索性能和樣本高效適應的框架。<lb/>EAR 結合了兩種機制：探索性反思，它通過迭代搜索來啟動檢索並為每個查詢收集有用的經驗；以及同化反思，它從經驗緩衝區重播這些經驗，以比僅依賴即時獎勵的方法更高效地完善全局重排器。<lb/>實驗表明，EAR 在兩個長期對話基準上使檢索性能比基線檢索器提高了最多 17.9%。<lb/>我們還顯示了 EAR 在樣本效率和對噪聲反饋的穩健性方面表現優異。
